company_name: Millennium & Copthorne Hotels New Zealand Limited

equity_bridge.item: 65.05% stake in CDI.NZ at CDI's own house weighted IV (NZD 0.4051/share x 292.672m shares x 65.05%)
equity_bridge.note: CDI.NZ_DCF.json probability_weighted.weighted_iv; CDI valued separately under its own NTA/P-B/P-E blended model per CDI.NZ memory entry, avoiding double-counting cyclical land-development earnings inside this hotel-only DCF. Stake % per H1-2026 investor presentation (65.05%); FY2025 annual report related-party note showed 65.12% - immaterial difference, current figure used.

equity_bridge.item: 50% Sofitel Brisbane Central JV, book carrying value
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 annual report note 22, 'Investment in joint venture'; equity-accounted, profit share (NZD 2.639m FY2025) excluded from operating flows above (sits below operating profit, not consolidated) - carrying value added here as the matching asset per owner-fcf-adaptations.md section (d). Conservative: no premium applied despite the JV's improving trajectory (event-driven Brisbane demand ahead of the 2032 Olympics) and no minority discount either, given it is a controlled 50/50 JV with the ultimate parent CDL/Accor group.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: hotel-only residual revenue (MCK consolidated less CDI.NZ reported revenue) FY2022-FY2025: $77.1m -> $114.9m -> $127.1m -> $148.6m, a 24.5% 3yr CAGR - but this period is dominated by the refurbishment-driven room-inventory unlock (rooms coming back online after multi-year closures for Revive to Thrive) and is NOT a sustainable run-rate. selected_growth_rate of 8% for the base-case Y1 driver instead anchors to H1 FY2026's +15.3% NZ hotel revenue growth, tapering hard toward a long-run NZ tourism/RevPAR growth rate of 2.5-3% as the inventory-unlock tailwind exhausts (refurbishment programme is now substantially complete per FY2025/H1-2026 commentary).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity and EPS CAGRs are not computable on a comparable ex-CDI, ex-one-off basis (equity series breaks at the FY2021 hotel-property revaluation-to-cost-model restatement per adjudication notes, FY2022 is a sparse one-page-summary year, and FY2024 NPAT includes a one-off $25.8m non-cash deferred-tax charge) - selected_growth_rate is therefore anchored to the hotel-only revenue residual and current-year guidance/trading momentum rather than a blended long-run equity CAGR, consistent with the mid-cycle/component-build approach used for the capex and margin paths.

scenario_narratives.base: The refurbishment-driven inventory unlock fades into a normal, moderate NZ hotel growth trajectory; margins recover from the current disrupted level to a mature 25% as capex normalizes off its FY2025 supercycle peak.
scenario_narratives.bull: Tourism recovery, City Rail Link, and the loyalty programme drive above-trend ADR/occupancy with full margin recapture to 29%, plus optionality from the Downtown Carpark and Queenstown Lakefront developments not modelled in the base flows.
scenario_narratives.bear: Domestic/corporate travel softness persists, capex stays structurally elevated (seismic, aged-infrastructure), margin recovery stalls at 18%, and the ~84%-controlled, ~16%-free-float governance structure caps any re-rating regardless of operating performance.

valuation_philosophy.summary: MCK is valued as a sum-of-parts: (1) the hotel/rental/Zenith operating business on an owner-FCF DCF, mid-cycle normalized because FY2024-25 capex and FCF are depressed by a near-complete refurbishment supercycle (hotel-only capex ran ~35% of revenue in FY2025 versus a 5-8% historical norm) rather than a steady-state signal - this Drivers file backs CDI.NZ's own reported revenue/EBITDA/capex/FCF out of MCK's consolidated figures each year (FY2022-FY2025) to isolate the hotel residual; (2) MCK's 65.05% stake in CDL Investments NZ (CDI.NZ), added via the equity bridge at CDI's own separately-published house DCF value rather than blended into the hotel margin/growth path, since CDI is a structurally distinct, highly cyclical NZ land-development business; (3) the 50%-owned, equity-accounted Sofitel Brisbane Central JV, added at book carrying value since its profit is excluded from operating flows. This mirrors the sum-of-parts precedent used for TGG.NZ and GXH.NZ in this research folder. A first-principles NTA/market-value cross-check exists independently of this DCF: management's own FY2025 disclosure puts fair-market-value net asset backing at NZD 5.24/share (book NTA NZD 3.66/share at H1 FY2026), and Northington Partners' independent valuation during the 2025 takeover defense assessed control value at NZD 4.40-5.00/share (midpoint 4.70) versus the failed NZD 2.80/share offer - both sit well above this DCF's weighted intrinsic value, which is unsurprising for a controlled company where minorities cannot access asset-backing value directly (no mechanism to force a sale, wind-up or a fresh full-value offer).
key_risks_to_valuation: CDLHH NZ's ~84% ordinary shareholding (over 91% of preference shares) with no disclosed near-term intention to launch a fresh Takeovers Code offer since its self-imposed standstill lapsed around January 2026 - minority holders have no mechanism to force any value-realising event, so this DCF's per-share value may simply never be realised in a transaction
Ongoing Takeovers Code 'creep' capacity (up to 5% of ordinary shares per rolling 12 months) that can keep eroding the already-thin ~16% free float and liquidity over time

Related-party transactions with the CDL/Hong Leong Group (the Grand Millennium Auckland ground lease renewed November 2025 with a Group-affiliated landlord) compound governance-quality concerns already flagged by the November 2023 NZMDT public censure for Audit Committee composition and disclosure breaches

The hotel-only revenue/EBITDA residual used as the DCF base is derived by subtracting CDI.NZ's own reported figures from MCK's consolidated figures - this is an approximation (it does not isolate minor items like the 49%-consolidated Copthorne Bay of Islands JV or small intra-group eliminations) rather than a segment note MCK itself discloses at this granularity

CDI.NZ's own valuation (the largest single equity-bridge item, ~NZD 77m) is itself subject to NZ residential land-cycle risk, which H1 FY2026 commentary described as 'more subdued than envisaged' - a further CDI derating would flow directly through the bridge

Capex normalization is a base-case assumption, not a certainty: seismic assessment/strengthening at Copthorne Wellington Oriental Bay and further aged-infrastructure replacement could keep hotel capex elevated well beyond the modelled 6.5-7% steady state, which is the bear case's central driver

data_sources.financials: MCK.NZ_Metrics.csv (core_metrics/metrics_normalized), MCK.NZ.duckdb kpis table, MCK.NZ_Annual_FY2025.txt and MCK.NZ_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt cash-flow/segment/JV notes, CDI.NZ_Metrics.csv and CDI.NZ_DCF.json for the CDI residual and stake valuation

inputs.sbc_source: unavailable - no SBC scheme disclosed in filings; MCK is ~84% controlled, no equity award programme found. sbc_pct held at 0 (SBC-zero market per owner-fcf-adaptations.md section e)
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.5% built on NZD risk-free ~4.6% (NZGB 10yr) + ERP ~6.5% for a small-cap NZ real-estate-heavy operator, before any illiquidity/governance discount (that risk is charged once, via the bear-scenario weight and the entry-price hurdle, not stacked into WACC per adaptations section 7f)
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A) - leases as debt. Lease payments are immaterial (Group lease principal only $2.3m/yr in financing activities FY2025, mostly the Grand Millennium Auckland ground lease and minor equipment leases; most hotels are owned freehold). Lease liabilities ($26.927m, FY2025 Group figure, used as latest available) included once in the net-debt bridge; NOT deducted a second time from operating flows, since the component EBITDA/capex build below excludes financing-activity lease principal by construction.
inputs.nci_treatment: Sum-of-parts, not a blended NCI leakage rate. MCK's ~65.05% owned land-developer subsidiary CDL Investments NZ (CDI.NZ) is backed OUT of the flow build entirely (consolidated MCK revenue/EBITDA/capex/FCF less CDI's own reported revenue/EBITDA/capex/FCF, both from each company's audited FY2022-FY2025 figures) so this DCF prices the hotel/rental/Zenith operating business only, on a 100%-owned-equivalent basis (residual NCI in the hotel segment itself - e.g. the 49%-held but consolidated Copthorne Bay of Islands JV - is small and left inside the residual as an approximation; it does not move the answer materially). MCK's 65.05% stake in CDI is added into the equity bridge at CDI's OWN probability-weighted DCF value (CDI.NZ_DCF.json, weighted_iv NZD 0.4051/share x 292.672m shares x 65.05% = NZD 77.1m), avoiding double-counting CDI's cyclical land-development earnings inside a hotel-business margin/growth path. The 50%-owned, equity-accounted Sofitel Brisbane Central JV is excluded from operating flows (its profit share sits below operating profit and is not in the residual) and its book carrying value (NZD 51.209m, FY2025) is added to the bridge instead - the matching-asset rule for excluded income (adaptations section d).
inputs.notes: Routed via SKILL.md as a sum-of-parts: (1) hotel/rental/Zenith operating business valued as an owner-FCF DCF (this Drivers file), mid-cycle-normalized because FY2024-25 capex/FCF are depressed by the near-complete 'Revive to Thrive' refurbishment supercycle (FY2025 hotel-only capex ~35% of revenue vs a pre-supercycle norm of 5-8%, e.g. FY2019 group capex 3.0% of revenue) - see historical_growth.notes; (2) MCK's 65.05% stake in CDI.NZ valued at CDI's own house DCF and added via equity_bridge; (3) the 50% Sofitel Brisbane JV added at book carrying value via equity_bridge. FY2024's NPAT was additionally depressed by a one-off $25.8m non-cash deferred-tax charge (building-depreciation deductibility removal) - not relevant to this owner-FCF build, which starts from EBITDA, but noted for completeness since it affects any P/E-based sanity check. Net debt uses total_debt=lease liabilities only (bank debt is $0 at H1 FY2026, the latest balance-sheet date) minus cash; MCK's own bank borrowings were repaid to zero during H1 FY2026, a real de-gearing signal supporting the mid-cycle margin recovery thesis. Governance/illiquidity risk (CDLHH NZ ~84% control, ~16% free float, Takeovers Code creep provision, no mechanism for minorities to force a value-realising event) is charged through the bear-scenario weight (30%, above the 15% house default) and flagged explicitly in valuation_philosophy - NOT through a WACC premium, to avoid charging the same risk twice.

bear.narrative: Bear case: management's own H1 FY2026 commentary already flags 'softer domestic consumer and corporate travel as fiscal conditions bite' and geopolitical/fuel-shortage disruption to international arrivals; growth stalls near 1.5-2%/yr, refurbished rooms fail to lift margin back to historical levels (seismic remediation at Copthorne Wellington Oriental Bay and further aged-infrastructure replacement keep capex elevated for longer, at 8% of revenue even at steady state, versus 6.5% base), and the structural governance/illiquidity overhang (CDLHH NZ ~84% control, ~16% free float, no minority mechanism to force a value-realising event, dividend policy at the controlling shareholder's discretion) caps any re-rating - terminal cap held to 11x. WACC held equal to base (risk is charged in the flows and the bear weight, not stacked into a higher bear discount rate, per owner-fcf-adaptations.md section 7f).

base.narrative: Base case: the 'Revive to Thrive' refurbishment programme is substantially complete (Queenstown, Rotorua, Bay of Islands done in FY2025; Grand Millennium Auckland renovations done by end-2025), so capex decelerates from the FY2025 supercycle peak (35% of hotel-only revenue) toward a normal maintenance/growth level of 6.5-7% by year 4-5, while EBITDA margin recovers from FY2025's refurb-disrupted 18.5% toward a 25% mature level as occupancy holds near 100% of available rooms, the Mayfair Christchurch acquisition contributes a full year, and the renewed Grand Millennium Auckland lease and City Rail Link opening support Auckland demand. Revenue growth starts at 8% (below H1 FY2026's +15.3% actual, reflecting the inventory-unlock tailwind fading) and decelerates to a 2.5% long-run NZ tourism/RevPAR growth rate by year 8.

bull.narrative: Bull case: NZ inbound tourism recovery accelerates further (RevPAR already +13.6% YTD June 2026), the Auckland City Rail Link opening and My Millennium loyalty programme drive above-trend ADR/occupancy gains, the Downtown Carpark and Queenstown Lakefront developments add incremental owned room/asset value, and the Sofitel Brisbane JV benefits from a strong multi-year events calendar (Lions tour, State of Origin, Ashes, then the 2027 Rugby World Cup and 2032 Olympics build-up) - none of which is in the base flow (JV profit excluded from operating flows), so bull upside here is purely the core hotel business exceeding its own recovery trajectory with a full margin recapture to 29% and modest re-rating headroom (16x cap).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised to 30% (above the 15% house default) for the structural governance/illiquidity risk that is specific to this ticker and cannot be diversified away by an operating recovery: CDLHH NZ's ~84% control with no obligation or stated near-term intention to make a further offer, a Takeovers Code creep provision that can keep eroding the ~16% free float, and no mechanism for minority holders to force a distribution increase or exit event even if the hotel business itself performs well - this is charged here, in the scenario weight, rather than as a WACC premium, per the 'charge risk once' rule. Bull weight trimmed to 20% because it requires both an operating outcome (margin recapture to 29%, full inventory monetisation) AND a re-rating that a governance-constrained, thinly-traded stock may simply never receive.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
